children: Royal Caribbean Group is nearing a deal to acquire Sandals Resorts International, the Financial Times reported Tuesday. Traders soured on the potential transaction, which would rank as the cruise operator's largest in its history.
Shares of Royal Caribbean fell 6.17% to $234.81, their lowest close since hitting $233.25 on May 9. The broader S&P 500 was flat.

An acquisition by Royal Caribbean would value Sandals at more than $6 billion and grant the cruise operator control of 20 resorts across the Caribbean. Members of the controlling Stewart family would retain equity holdings as part of the deal, while Royal Caribbean would have the ability to take full ownership later.
A deal could be announced within days even as talks are ongoing, FT reported.
Royal Caribbean did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Barron's.

The Stewart family has explored a potential sale of Sandals on and off for years, with prior efforts failing to produce a deal. In June, CEO Adam Stewart ruled out any sale of the company and said that Sandals was seeking capital for expansion, not an exit.
In April, Royal Caribbean projected that rising oil prices would cut into its full-year earnings, and that war in the Middle East would curtail voyages in the region.

Investors had been fearing a worsening environment for Royal Caribbean and other cruise firms because of the Iran conflict, but at the end of July the company reported better-than-expected earnings through its second quarter, which it attributed to strong last-minute demand and lower costs.
